overview: Some bacteria were never going to respond to a given antibiotic; others start out susceptible and change.
genZNote: Born resistant versus resistant because it picked up the memo.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Natural, inherent resistance possessed by essentially all members of a species or genus, independent of prior antibiotic exposure.
aspects.valueB: Resistance that develops in a previously susceptible organism, through mutation or acquisition of new genetic material.

aspects.label: Genetic Basis
aspects.valueA: Encoded on the core chromosome, a stable and universal species trait (e.g. an outer membrane that excludes a drug).
aspects.valueB: Arises from spontaneous chromosomal mutation or acquisition of mobile genetic elements (plasmids, transposons).

aspects.label: Predictability
aspects.valueA: Fully predictable — every strain of the species will be resistant, so susceptibility testing for that drug is not performed.
aspects.valueB: Unpredictable at the species level — must be tested for individually in each isolate, since some strains are resistant and others are not.

aspects.label: Mechanism Examples
aspects.valueA: Absence of the drug's target, an impermeable outer membrane, or a constitutive efflux pump.
aspects.valueB: New enzyme production (e.g. beta-lactamase), altered target site by mutation, acquired efflux pump upregulation.

aspects.label: Classic Examples
aspects.valueA: Vancomycin against Gram-negative bacteria (can't cross the outer membrane).
aspects.valueB: Methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) via acquisition of the mecA gene.

aspects.label: Spread Potential
aspects.valueA: Not transferable — it's simply part of what the species is.
aspects.valueB: Can spread horizontally between bacteria via plasmids, contributing to outbreak-level resistance.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Universal to the species, not tested for individually.
aspects.valueB: Variable between strains, must be tested for and can spread horizontally.
